newsitem.title: MONACO: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO V MARSEILLE FACTS AND FIGURES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MONACO V MARSEILLE FACTS AND FIGURES.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's French first division match between Monaco and Marseille at the Louis II stadium.
Monaco: Founded in 1924 as Association Sportive de Monaco, joined French league as a professional team in 1948. They have won the French first division championship five times.
Major honours: League champions: 1961, 1963, 1978, 1982, 1988. French Cup winners: 1960, 1963, 1980, 1985, 1991.
Ground: Stade Louis II, capacity 18,500 (15,000 seated). Record number of spectators: 22,000 v AS Roma of Italy in March 1992.
Trainer: Jean Tigana.
Record league appearances: Jean-Luc Ettori 602.
Record number of goals: Delio Onnis 157.
Marseille: Founded in 1899 as Olympique de Marseille. They have won the French league title eight times.

Major honours: League champions: 1937, 1948, 1971, 1972, 1989, 1990, 1991, 1992 (also 1993, but stripped of title over match-rigging scandal). French Cup winners: 1924, 1926, 1927, 1935, 1938, 1943, 1969, 1972, 1976, 1989. European Cup: 1993.
Ground: Stade Velodrome, capacity 46,000. Record number of spectators: 48,039 v Ajax Amsterdam, October 20, 1972 in the European Cup.
Trainer: Gerard Gili.
Record league appearances: Roger Scotti 360.
Record number of goals: Gunnar Andersson 169.
Monaco v Marseille league meetings at Stade Louis II in last five years: 0-3 (1991/2), 1-0 (1992/3), 0-0 (1993/4).
Fascinating facts:
- Monaco president Jean-Louis Campora, a 55-year-old doctor who also presides over the principality's parliament, has been in charge of the club for 22 years.
- Monaco belong to a second wave of French clubs founded between the two world wars (the first wave came at the turn of the century).

- Monaco made a qualitative leap under current Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger in the late 1980s and early 1990s when they became regular qualifiers for European competition and reached the 1992 Cup Winners' Cup final.

- They almost always play against bigger crowds away than at home where their average last season was just over 6,000, a third of the capacity at the Stade Louis II. But football followers in the principality claim it is not indifference and that such an average is good when they are drawing on a population of only 30,000 and environs boosting the figure to no more than 100,000.
- Monaco have an annual budget of 110 million francs ($22 million), about half of which comes from a state subsidy.

- Marseille beat Monaco 3-1 at the Velodrome in their first league clash of the season in November. Monaco, then second six points behind Paris St Germain, have lost two league matches in 17 since and are now top, 11 points ahead of PSG.

- Marseille are yet to win away this season. Only once in their history have they finished a season without an away victory, in 1958/9 when they drew five times and lost 14 on the road and were relegated for the first time. They have three away games in which to try to avoid a repeat of the record, at Monaco, Lens and Lyon, although they are out of danger of relegation.
- Marseille, 12th in the first division standings, were never lower than sixth in the eight seasons since 1986 prior to their enforced relegation over the 1993 match-rigging scandal.

- Marseille have not been relegated for strictly playing reasons since 1982. Their relegation in 1994 was ordered by the French league over the Valenciennes match-rigging scandal. They won promotion straight back as 1995 second division champions but were not allowed to benefit from it, being relegated for a second consecutive season for financial irregularities.
